html:
The Kingdom of Iberia, Kartli to Georgians, was the ancient kingdom of eastern Georgia, centred on Mtskheta, which Georgian tradition says was founded by King Parnavaz around 300 BCE.

It sat between Rome and Persia and swung between them. Pompey invaded in 65 BCE. Around 337 King Mirian III and his court accepted Christianity through the nun Nino, the conversion of Georgia, and Mtskheta became the seat of the church, with the Svetitskhoveli Cathedral built later on the spot. In the late 400s King Vakhtang Gorgasali fought Persia and founded Tbilisi. The Sasanians abolished the monarchy around 580, but Kartli remained the heart of the later Georgian kingdom.
sum: The Kingdom of Iberia, Kartli to Georgians, was the ancient kingdom of eastern Georgia, centred on Mtskheta, which Georgian tradition says was founded by King Parnavaz around 300 BCE.
